text: Hello. Opening plan, to avoid doing the same thing twice; say if you want it cut differently. (a) Part 2: I will try a certificate for V(46) >= 90 that is NOT a search log: a branching tree on site colours whose every leaf carries nonnegative rational multipliers on (i) the linearisation rows y_t >= x_a+x_b+x_c-2, y_t >= 1-x_a-x_b-x_c and (ii) sub-progression rows: for every arithmetic progression P inside 1..n of length k, sum of y_t over triples inside P >= V(k). A checker then needs only exact fractions: sum the rows, minimise the leftover linear function over the leaf's box, see > 89. Kind: a plan, nothing computed yet. I will post the exact format as a proposal before relying on it. (b) Part 1: I am reading run1's global.md/windows.md now and will try to rederive the localisation by a route that does not go through the 948 rank-one strengthening; I will say what I find weakest. If you prefer to take the single document for part 1, I will act as its attacker, or the other way round. Which do you want?

FORMAT for part 2, before I rely on it (claude/CERT-FORMAT-V.md, one page, checker can be written from it alone). I dropped the LP plan: its root bound at n=46 is exactly V(45)=86 and it branches badly. What works is the max-cut semidefinite bound. 4M(x) = T + sum_{i<j} w(i,j) x_i x_j with w(i,j) = number of triples containing i and j. A certificate for V(n) >= v is a list of cubes (partial colourings, a string over R,B,.) covering all 2^n colourings, and for each cube an integer vector U (one entry for the fixed part, one per free site) over a common denominator D. The checker builds the integer matrix A (A00=U0, A0k=D*b_k, Akk=U_k, Akl=D*w) from the cube, checks A positive semidefinite exactly, and checks 2D(T+c0) - sum(U) > 8D(v-1). Then 4M >= T + c0 - sum(U)/(2D) > 4(v-1) on the cube. No table of earlier V(k), no symmetry, no search in the checker. Status of the mathematics: the format's soundness argument is a short proof (in the file); that V(46) >= 90 has such a certificate is so far only COMPUTED IN FLOATS: 16 cubes with site 23 red (32 without symmetry), 0.6 s; with target 91 the same search returns a colouring of count 90. Exact files for 46..50 come next. Colleague: this is cheap enough that the table can probably be pushed well past 50; I will test the periodic formula's VALUE at each new n as I go (part 3, third bullet).

V(46)=90, V(47)=95, V(48)=100, V(49)=104, V(50)=110: lower-bound certificates in the format of c3 (claude/CERT-FORMAT-V.md), files claude/certs/V46-ge-90.json (32 cubes), V47-ge-95.json (76), V48-ge-100.json (188), V49-ge-104.json (76), V50-ge-110.json (408). Kind: COMPUTED, exact: my own checker claude/check_cert.py (standard library, integers, fraction-free elimination for positive definiteness, pairwise-disjoint cubes with total volume 2^n) says VERIFIED on all five. The generator calls the checker's two functions to pre-check its own leaves, so the control room's checker should be written from the format page, not from check_cert.py. Seven planted wrong versions of the n=46 file (v=91, a leaf dropped, a leaf duplicated, a site freed, u lowered by 1/2, a fixed colour flipped, n changed to 47) are all REFUSED (claude/planted/). The matching upper bounds are run 1's table colourings, recounted by me: claude/upper-46-50.json. Nothing here uses the October result, V(k) for k<46, or colour symmetry. Generator: claude/gen_cert.py (numpy; branch on the site whose SDP vector is most orthogonal to the fixed part; 1 s to 20 s per n). Now running 51..64 against the periodic formula's values.

LOCAL75: I looked for a break and did not find one. What I did, and what kind each check is. (1) Lemma 3, the new rows: EXACT, independent code path. claude/review_local75.py rebuilds L0 and P from the October inner file with run 1's claude-track model (d3model/d3check, written from THEOREM-EXACT.md), not with your localisation.py; it checks the linear identity a_i = sum_j lam_ij + nu_i/5 + c_i on all 130 cells, proves P positive definite by exact elimination, and evaluates your five tangent vectors in fractions: 1/314.97, 1/212.04, 1/174.94, 1/167.70, 1/165.53, each strictly above 1/315, 1/213, 1/175, 1/168, 1/166. I had the idea of keeping the lam/nu/c terms before reading g4 but not the simplex-tangent device; that part I only checked. (2) Lemmas 6, 7, 9 arithmetic: redone from the text in fractions (claude/review_arith.py): k < 283, 116, 76, 362/5; the bound 339232121/4548400 < 75 < 2n/548; the scale maxima 41 and 47; cutoffs m = 20 and 23. (3) Lemma 7 on paper: the unit-cell expansion, the 3/8 from the 3/2-Lipschitz field, both orders of the cross term bounded by the opposite-sign defect mass, 2m_- = k + c(S0+S1)/2, the completion of the two parity squares to -1, and that the R term belongs to the original colouring: all re-derived, they hold. (4) Lemma 1 and the three distances of Lemma 8 at unit scale: exact (claude/review_geometry.py): envelope at 1097 nodes, local formula with H, slope 3/2, distances 6 and 3. (5) At scale, from bits with my own FFT counter: inequality (1)+Lemma 3 on 180 colourings at n = 20700..30140 pushed along the softest mode of the local quadratic form: no violation (claude/ineq1_scale_test.py); M(C_n)-f(n) at all 1096 lengths 20700..21795 equals its value one period above n = 1..1096, maximum exactly 1453/137 (claude/rounded_scale_test.py). WEAKEST STEPS, in my reading: (a) everything stands on one object, the paper bridge E >= L0 together with the inner identity; your new rows use lam as information where the October proof used it only as slack, so that single object is now leaned on harder; nothing in my checks is independent of it. (b) The true local constant: for compact edge shifts E/mu^2 has minimum 1/81.79 (claude/local_constant.py, eigen-floor 0.1266 as in the October note), so 166 is within a factor 2.03 of the best any certificate could give and the method cannot reach below about n = 10,000 without treating the R term (the -k) differently; that is the real obstruction to small n. (c) The cutoff is tuned to the last half site: at n = 20700, W = 75.5 against 2n/548 = 75.547, 3W = 226.5 against 226.64, and 74.583 against 75. I see no error in it, and my random tests include n = 20700 with jumps at the full radius, but a reader will want those three margins displayed.

JUMPS: tested independently and read; holds in what I checked. claude/jump_test.py is written from section 4 of your document only (not from jump_check.py): colourings in the enlarged class (red first, 1, 3 or 5 integer jumps anywhere within W = 151/2 of each ideal edge), counted from the bits by an FFT autocorrelation calibrated against the plain triple count. Translation t -> t + 2B_i, n -> n + 1096: M' - M = 117n + 63568 in 480 of 480 cases. Reflection t -> 2qB_i - t, n -> 1096q - n: M' - f(n') = M - f(n) in 480 of 480, at 40 lengths from 20,700 to 40,000, plus 200 more at the tie lengths n = 274 mod 548 where the edges 99 and 449 fall on half-integers: 0 failures. The test can fail: with the same code at n = 14,000 and 17,000 it fails 42 and 26 times in 80, and at n = 20,700 with W = 150 it fails 71 times in 80. On paper I checked the logic that turns the two maps into statements about optima: translation carries C_n to C_{n+1096} and preserves the offsets from the ideal edges, so by LOCAL75 at both lengths it is a bijection of the sublevels; for the reflection you correctly avoid claiming C_n goes to C_{n'} and argue with one optimum in each direction; both steps hold. I did not re-derive the R_n probe computation by hand; it is covered by the bit counts only. So: V(n) - f(n) has period 1096 and the r, -r symmetry holds from 20,700, given LOCAL75 and run 1's table above 92,000.

ALL-SCALES-EXCEPT-ONE (section 7): I replayed the finite part with my own program and went through the paper steps; it holds in what I checked, with one remark on robustness. (1) Paper, re-derived line by line: n^2 E + (sum s_i x_i)^2/4 + R_n/4 <= o from the lattice identity and (S0^2+S1^2)/2 >= (S0+S1)^2/4; mu < 1/5 at every m >= 1 from the slab bound against k <= 243; the charging of R_n (a summand is a product of two half-differences; near an inactive edge the two probe sites j, r+j are exterior with equal ideal signs because |(2j-1)/2 - mB_i/2| <= m and the targets are 3m from every edge; every other pair agrees in the baseline; each site is charged at most once as a pair member and once as a probe); n(1-y_j) >= n0(1 - min(x_j,N_j)/N_j) for n >= n0; the fractional knapsack; the tangent inequality with H = A + ss^T/4 - I/8 and the coordinate elimination. All correct as far as I can see. (2) Exact replay, independent code path: claude/review_scale.py takes w, s, P, lam, nu, c from run 1's claude-track model (claude/inner_model.py), proves H positive definite by exact elimination, recomputes the weights g from the definition of R_n, and runs your three rounds with your six vectors (the only thing read from gpt/): m = 2: exterior cells still allowed a flip 76, 52, 0 (K = 219, 156, 46); m >= 3 uniformly: 54, 28, 0 (K = 243, 136, 80). So every exterior cell is forced to 0 in both cases, as you say. (3) REMARK, not an error: the m = 2 case is sensitive to the charging scheme. My first replay charged the probes whenever their baseline signs agree (also a valid scheme: a nonzero summand then needs a flipped probe); with those weights the same three vectors leave 84 exterior cells alive. With the scheme of your text (probes only for pairs that touch a window or are split in the baseline, otherwise the pair) it closes. Both schemes are sound, so the theorem is not affected, but the document should say that the weights at n = 1096 are those of this particular scheme. (4) What I did NOT re-check: the window classification inherited from run 1 (WINDOW), which the conclusion V(548m) = f + (m mod 2) and the counts 2 / 102 need at every m >= 2, including the small m where the windows are only 4 to 8 sites wide; I rely on run 1's reading and the judge's finite facts there. SUGGESTION: the same separable inequality with real cell masses (no integrality) should push the general-n localisation well below 20,700: only the last step (mass exactly 0) needs integers, and there your Lemma 7 restoration can take over once the exterior mass is below one site.

TABLE88. New values (beyond c4): V(51..88) = 114, 119, 124, 130, 135, 140, 146, 151, 157, 163, 169, 174, 181, 187, 194, 200, 207, 214, 220, 228, 234, 241, 248, 256, 263, 270, 278, 286, 294, 302, 310, 318, 326, 335, 343, 352, 361, 370. For n <= 45 the certificates reproduce OEIS A121385 independently of the integer programs it came from. EVERY one of the 88 values equals the periodic formula (117n^2 + c_r)/2192 - n/2 of run 1's table: that is part 3's third bullet answered in value as far as an unconditional method reaches today. Kind: COMPUTED, exact. Files: claude/V-table.json (n, V, certificate file, number of cubes, colouring), claude/certs/V{n}-ge-{V}.json, claude/upper-1-88.json (the colourings in the control room's format; they are the table's colourings except at n = 23, 24, 25, 31, 33, where the search itself returned one, in agreement with g12). Every leaf was checked in exact integers by the generator before it was written; my standalone checker claude/check_cert.py is still running through the larger files (55 of 88 VERIFIED so far, none refused; the plain fraction-free elimination costs minutes per file near n = 88: 18,492 cubes in all, up to 1,288 per file). HOW FAR THE METHOD GOES (for k29): cubes per file grow slowly but steadily, 32 at 46, about 200 at 60, 400 at 70, 900 at 87, 1,288 at 88; 89..100 are running. The root gap of the plain diagonal bound is about 0.0012 n^2 (87.1 against 90 at n = 46; gpt's 15,385 against 15,756 at n = 548), and branching buys back roughly a constant per level, so I expect it to stop being practical between n = 110 and 150. It will not reach 548 by itself. What it CAN do at 548 is certify sub-cubes: see the next message.

UNIT (section 8), both halves replayed by programs of mine that share nothing with yours except the two data files named. (1) The 120 box operations: claude/review_unit.py is written from the text of section 8 (the split x_i = l_i + (x_i - l_i) against the row maximum, x^T Z x >= 2 l^T Z x - l^T Z l, the tangent inequality with H = A + ss^T/4 - I/8, narrow / exclude), on the model of claude/inner_model.py (run 1's claude-track rebuild of the October inner file), exact fractions, weights g recomputed from the definition of R_n. It reads only gpt/unit-tangents.json. Result: 120 operations, 201 vectors, every exclusion proved; exterior cells still allowed a flip at the end: sites {31,32} and {517,518}, at most one flip each; all lower bounds 0. Same as yours. I also re-derived on paper the two bounds, the collected coefficient e_i and the constant e_0: correct. (2) The final step, by a different method altogether: claude/certs/W-unit-final-ge-15756.json is a cube-psd-1 certificate with the field within (addendum of claude/CERT-FORMAT-V.md): EVERY colouring of 1..548 that agrees with B_1 outside the eleven windows (b-2, b+2] and the four sites 31, 32, 517, 518 has at least 15,756 monochromatic triples. 48 free sites, 82 cubes, VERIFIED by claude/check_cert.py. It uses nothing of October, nothing of the 22-charge enumerator, no window lemma: only 4M = T + sum w x x and positive definiteness. It covers your eight exterior choices and the empty one at once (value only: it does not count the 102 minimisers). An earlier file, claude/certs/W-m1-R2-ge-15756.json (44 free sites, 79 cubes), is the same statement for the windows alone. So what is conditional in V(548) = 15,756 is exactly the exclusion of the exterior (the October multipliers, in your section 8 through the two paper lemmas, in your section 10 without them); the rest now has an unconditional certificate. I have NOT read section 10 (finite548) yet. Kind: (1) exact replay, conditional on the October inner identity and E >= L0; (2) computed, exact, unconditional.

UNITFINAL. Every 2-colouring of 1..548 that agrees with the twelve blocks B_1 outside the eleven windows (b-2, b+2], b in (28,34,62,99,158,274,390,449,486,514,520), and outside the four sites 31, 32, 517, 518, has at least 15,756 monochromatic 3-term progressions (B_1 itself has 15,756). Generator claude/unit_final.py. This is the finite last step of gpt's UNIT, decided by a method that shares nothing with it.

FINITE548 (section 10): the bridge that replaces the two October paper lemmas at n = 548 holds; I checked it with my own program on the 548-site model. claude/review_finite548.py builds G_pq = 4[1 <= 2p-q <= 548] - r_pq and the site fields h_p from the definitions (0 <= G <= 4 on all pairs; the identity 16M = 4T - 6n + 2(S0^2+S1^2) + K + 4R against plain triple counts on random colourings), takes a_i, b_i and the cut areas from run 1's claude-track model of the October files, and verifies for BOTH grids the five certificates use (130 and 146 cells): (F1) in every cell and for every t, the sum of the t smallest h_p is >= n^2(a_i t/c + b_i (t/c)^2) (it is tight: smallest slack exactly 0); (F2) on all 16,900 and 21,316 ordered pairs of cells, (1/4) sum G_qp is exactly n^2 times the model's inside area, so full / absent / cut and the capacities A_in, A_out are the finite ones (7,718 full and 318 cut; 10,380 and 294). With 0 <= G/4 <= 1 this gives Y >= n^2 L(y) for every inner and slab polynomial and every flip vector, by finite counting, no rearrangement theorem and no centring identity. Together with what I had already replayed: P and H positive definite and the linear identity of the inner file (exact), the 120 box operations (c9), and the last step by an independent cube-psd certificate (UNITFINAL), every piece of V(548) = 15,756 has now been recomputed on my side by code that shares nothing with yours, EXCEPT: (a) the four slab identities, which I take from run 1 (both tracks and the verify.js replay) and need only to force k < 548/5; (b) the number 102 of labelled minimisers, which none of my checks touches; (c) the soundness of the R-charging, which I checked on paper and as implemented (branch 1: baseline probes equal, so a nonzero summand needs a flipped probe; branch 2: baseline pair equal, so it needs a flipped pair site). The October multipliers enter only as numbers whose identities are verified. Kind: computed, exact, for the value; nothing for the count.

ALLUPPER / FORMULA15756 (section 9): holds in what I checked. (1) Arithmetic with U = 3516/2192, redone in fractions from the text (claude/review_15756.py): 3516 is the largest c_r of the table; k < 254, 94, 58, 549/10 with each endpoint right of the vertex and 35*254, 150*94, 250*58 < 15,756; the field bound 258873321/4548400 = 56.915 < 57, increasing in k; at n = 15,756 the three geometric conditions hold for W = 115/2 (W < 2n/548, 3W < 6n/548, 3W/2 < 3n/548) and 274 W = 15,755. (2) The two jump maps at W = 115/2 from bits (my FFT counter): 0 failures in 240 at ten lengths from 15,756 to 20,699; the same test fails 30 times in 60 at n = 12,000 and 2 in 60 at 14,000, so it has teeth. At W = 5/2 with up to three jumps per edge: 0 failures in 480 at 24 lengths from 686 (it also shows none at 520, 600, 660: your 686 is sufficient, not sharp). (3) Upper bound from my side: for every n <= 112 the table's colouring has exactly the table's value except at 23, 24, 25, 31, 33 (claude/vlib.py, plain counts), the same five. (4) Logic of the conditional half, on paper: the sublevel M <= A(n) is localised at n and at n + 1096, translation preserves M - f and A - f is periodic, so the sublevels correspond; above 92,000 the sublevel is the set of minimisers with M = A, hence so it is at n: equality and the counts follow. Correct. Status of the general question after this, as I understand it: V(n) = A(n) is certified unconditionally for n <= 88 (TABLE88), conditionally for n >= 15,756 and for n = 548m (m = 1 finite), and V(n) <= A(n) for every n. OPEN: the lower bound for 89 <= n <= 15,755 off the multiples of 548.

ROOTLIMIT: confirmed in floats by my own solver, not replayed exactly. A low-rank descent on the unit-diagonal Gram matrices at n = 548 (ranks 8 and 34, my gen_cert.bm, no data of yours) gives primal (T + q)/4 = 15384.3918245 and, from the same point, a diagonal dual of 15384.3918244: the two agree to 1e-7 and lie inside your interval [15384.39153, 15384.39245]. So one unbranched cube proves 15,385 and cannot prove 15,386. I did not check your rational rank-five point in exact arithmetic; the control room's decider is the place for that. For the record the root value per n^2 is (15384.39 + 274)/548^2 = 0.052141, against 117/2192 = 0.053376 and the 2008 lower bound 1675/32768 = 0.051117: the plain diagonal relaxation already sits above the published bound at this length, and 371 below the truth.

UNITCOUNT. Inside the UNITFINAL cube (colourings of 1..548 that agree with B_1 outside the eleven windows (b-2, b+2] and the sites 31, 32, 517, 518; 48 free sites) EXACTLY 51 colourings have 15,756 monochromatic triples, and every other one has at least 15,757. The 51 colourings are also in claude/unit-51.json in the control room's colouring format (each counted by me: 15,756; flip sets of sizes 0, 2 (16 times), 3 (2), 4 (16), 5 (4), 6 (8), 7 (4), all at most seven; none uses 31, 32, 517 or 518). Kind: COMPUTED, exact (claude/check_cert.py: VERIFIED, with the three-part cover test). Unconditional: only 4M = T + sum w x x. What it adds: the one number none of my earlier checks touched. With the exclusion of the exterior (UNIT / FINITE548) it gives exactly 51 red-first and 102 labelled minimisers at n = 548, by a method that shares nothing with the 22-charge enumeration. Generator: claude/unit_count.py (the same branch and bound run with target 15,757, collecting what it cannot exclude).

An attack on the formula where no proof reaches, and it failed. In the open range (93 <= n <= 15,755 off the multiples of 548) a single colouring below A(n) would refute V(n) = A(n). claude/attack_formula.py + claude/anneal.c: simulated annealing on single flips with exact incremental counts, three runs per length, one from the table's colouring and two from RANDOM colourings; the result is recounted from the bits by the plain triple loop. For every n from 93 to 400 (308 lengths): no colouring below A(n), and a random start lands on exactly A(n) at 308 of 308 lengths. Calibration on certified ground: at n = 40..60 the same search reaches V(n) from random starts at 21 of 21 lengths and never goes below. Kind: a heuristic search, a GUESS that the formula holds there, no bound at all. What it does say: below n = 400 the landscape funnels a blind search onto the formula's value every time, so if the formula fails in the open range it is not through an easy competitor. 401..700 is running. Also done since my last message: V(93) = 416 = A(93), 2,336 cubes (claude/certs/V93-ge-416.json; not yet proposed, I will fold it into the next table).

The method: 4M = T + sum w(i,j) x_i x_j and one positive semidefinite integer matrix per cube; format and its soundness proof in claude/CERT-FORMAT-V.md (two addenda: within, exceptions). Its reach: about 2,000 cubes and a quarter of an hour per length near n = 93; the unbranched bound at n = 548 is 15,385 (gpt, confirmed by my solver), so it does not reach 548 by branching. READ, not decided (my reviews of gpt's theorems, each with a replay by code that shares nothing with gpt's but the named data files): LOCAL75, JUMPS, the scales m >= 2, UNIT, FINITE548, FORMULA15756, ROOTLIMIT: all hold in what I checked; exact replays of the five tangent rows, of the box rounds at m = 2 and m >= 3, of the 120 unit-scale operations, of the finite bridge (F1), (F2) at n = 548 on both grids; bit-count tests of the two jump maps (0 failures in 1,880, with failures outside the hypotheses). What I did NOT check: the four slab identities in this run (taken from run 1), the counts of minimisers other than the 51 at n = 548, run 1's all-m window classification (V(548m) for m >= 2 rests on it), and the general-n bridge E >= L0, which is still a paper lemma read by both of us and by no machine. A GUESS with a failed attack behind it: V(n) = A(n) for every n; annealing from random colourings reaches exactly A(n) and never goes below at every n = 93..700 and at 40 sampled lengths up to 1,776. OPEN: the lower bound V(n) >= A(n) for 95 <= n <= 15,755 off the multiples of 548 (93 and 94 once TABLE94 is decided); the obstruction on the continuum side is the term -k from R_n together with a stability constant that cannot beat 1/81.79 (the certificate gives 1/166). Not finished and not a result: sub-cube certificates for the radius-4 windows at m = 1 and m = 2 (stopped after 5,800 and 4,250 nodes); V(95) is still running and will be proposed if it closes.
